summary: Human demonstrations provide a rich source of bimanual dexterous skills, yet transferring them to robot hands remains challenging. Existing methods primarily optimize object trajectory tracking, often overlooking how human hands interact with the object.
takeaways: Across four benchmarks spanning three simulators and five robot embodiments, DexDuet improves object-tracking ADD-AUC by 11 to 41 points over the corresponding baselines while consistently achieving better contact preservation.
Existing methods primarily optimize object trajectory tracking, often overlooking how human hands interact with the object.
Even with accurate tracking, robots may contact incorrect object parts or slide their fingers, resulting in unstable manipulation.
